hyperedges.label: One coach-athlete pair is one relationship row
Equal gateway confirmation creates one access period
OTP acceptance of an invitation creates the active relationship
Paid Order Opens One Access Period

nodes.label: npx concurrently -c \"#93c5fd,#c4b5fd,#fb7185,#fdba74\" \"php artisan serve\" \"php artisan queue:listen --tries=1 --timeout=0\" \"php artisan pail --timeout=0\" \"npm run dev\" --names=server,queue,logs,vite --kill-others
nodes.norm_label: npx concurrently -c \"#93c5fd,#c4b5fd,#fb7185,#fdba74\" \"php artisan serve\" \"php artisan queue:listen --tries=1 --timeout=0\" \"php artisan pail --timeout=0\" \"npm run dev\" --names=server,queue,logs,vite --kill-others

nodes.label: Athlete Invitation
nodes.rationale: The coach records phone, name, and national code. If the person is not in the system, the account, athlete profile, and relationship are created in one transaction and an SMS is sent: registered by the coach, username is the phone, initial password is the national code. If the account exists, only the relationship is connected and the password is not changed. A duplicate phone for the same coach returns the open invitation, does not create a new invitation when a relationship is active, and uses reactivation when the relationship has ended.

nodes.label: Body Photo Access
nodes.rationale: Body photos exist in this version. The coach or the athlete stores them, and AI may see them during an active contract. After the contract ends, the coach and that coach's AI lose access.

nodes.label: Coaching Relationship
nodes.rationale: An active coaching_relationships row is the permission to program, give feedback, and see data for that collaboration. One pair of coach and athlete is one row; ending and starting again updates that row.

nodes.label: Epley v1 Estimated One-Rep Max
nodes.rationale: When an exercise has weight and reps, an estimated one-rep max using epley_v1 may be a separate event. It does not replace the primary record.

nodes.label: Feedback
nodes.rationale: The athlete records difficulty, pain, or a limitation and the coach replies. The subject is a performed session, a prescribed program item, an exercise, or a general topic of that relationship.

nodes.label: Free Workout Session
nodes.rationale: An athlete may log a free session outside the prescribed program and send it to the coach. It affects analysis of that relationship but does not change the training program. A session started after the relationship ends does not receive that relationship id.

nodes.label: In-App Notifications
nodes.rationale: Notifications are stored for a new program, a new record, a new analysis, and a feedback reply. This domain is not a realtime messenger.

nodes.label: athlete_invitations
nodes.rationale: An invitation before or alongside a relationship. pending_key is unique and equals coach id plus phone only while pending, so an open invite for the same coach and phone returns the same row. Proposed expiry is 7 days. Status is pending, accepted, expired, revoked, or declined.

nodes.label: bmi_v1
nodes.rationale: Versioned BMI formula. Calculated values use origin calculated and formula_code bmi_v1. A device value uses origin measured and can coexist.

nodes.label: body_metric_definitions
nodes.rationale: Vocabulary of metrics and units, not a report table. New girth codes are new vocabulary rows, not new observation columns. BMI may be measured or calculated.

nodes.label: body_observation_values
nodes.rationale: Only metrics that actually have a value. Unique on observation, metric, and origin so a device BMI and a calculated BMI can both exist. An unmeasured metric has no row. Before/After compares two observations and has no comparison-result table.

nodes.label: body_observations
nodes.rationale: One analysis entry. Visibility is athlete_private or relationship. A relationship-visible observation requires the relationship id and is not visible to another coach. A private observation has no relationship id. measured_at is the measurement time, not the insert time.

nodes.label: body_photos
nodes.rationale: Body-photo metadata. The file is on disk. The athlete always sees their own photos. The coach and that coach's AI see a photo only while the relationship is active and the photo carries that relationship id. Ending the relationship stops that read even for photos from the contract period. Photos are not deleted.

nodes.label: coaching_relationship_events
nodes.rationale: Append-only history of started, ended, and reactivated. Ending and starting again updates the relationship row and appends an event.

nodes.label: coaching_relationships
nodes.rationale: One relationship row per coach and athlete pair, unique on those two profiles. Status is active or ended. Equality of the two profile owners cannot be expressed simply in the database and is rejected in the acceptance transaction. A person cannot coach themselves.

nodes.label: epley_v1
nodes.rationale: Versioned estimated one-rep-max formula stored on a personal-record event as formula_code. It is an extra event and does not replace the primary metric.

nodes.label: feedback_messages
nodes.rationale: A shared message or an internal coach note. The athlete writes and reads only shared. coach_only is an internal note, not a conversation message.

nodes.label: feedback_threads
nodes.rationale: A feedback subject inside a relationship. At most one of session, prescribed item, or exercise is set. If none is set, the subject is general to the relationship. The subject must belong to that relationship. The rule is checked in the application because a multi-table CHECK is not practical in MySQL.

nodes.label: notifications
nodes.rationale: An in-app notification for program assigned, record achieved, body observation recorded, or feedback replied. subject has no foreign key because subjects differ. Push and websocket do not need another table.

nodes.label: personal_record_events
nodes.rationale: An append-only event when a metric exceeds the previous maximum for that athlete, exercise, and metric. Metrics are max weight, reps, duration, distance, or estimated one-rep max. Events are not updated.

nodes.label: workout_assignments
nodes.rationale: Assigns one published version to one relationship. The athlete profile must own that relationship. A new version does not by itself move an old assignment.

nodes.label: workout_day_exercises
nodes.rationale: A prescribed exercise. Tracking type may differ from the exercise default. The service does not write irrelevant metric columns. Target weight is optional for weight_reps. Duration exercises use only duration.

nodes.label: workout_days
nodes.rationale: A day or section of a version. Weekday may be null when the program is not tied to a weekday. The title can be a weekday session or full body.

nodes.label: workout_program_versions
nodes.rationale: An immutable version after publication. A published version and its children are not updated. Editing means the next draft. Publishing fills published_at and the service forbids later writes.

nodes.label: workout_programs
nodes.rationale: Stable identity of a training program owned by one coach. Status is draft, published, or archived.

nodes.label: workout_session_sets
nodes.rationale: A real set or attempt. sequence_no stays unique even when the prescribed item is null. An incomplete set does not create a record. exercise_id is copied at log time.

nodes.label: workout_sessions
nodes.rationale: A session that was actually performed. The relationship id is set only when the relationship is active at the start. Source is prescribed or athlete_free.

nodes.label: Create and Assign a Workout Program
nodes.rationale: A coach with the workout_programs capability creates a program and a draft version. Publishing freezes those rows. The next edit is a new draft, and current_version_id changes after the new version is published. Assignment points at the published version and the active relationship and creates a program_assigned notification. The old assignment still points at the previous version. Another coach's private exercise cannot be selected.
nodes.norm_label: create and assign a workout program

nodes.label: Body Analysis and Progress Report
nodes.rationale: An observation is stored for the measurement time. Only metrics that exist are inserted. If this observation has weight and a height exists here or on the latest earlier observation, a calculated bmi_centi row is added with bmi_v1. Relationship visibility carries the active relationship id and only that coach sees it with the athlete. Progress and Before/After read two times from these rows. No result table is created. A shared observation creates a body_observation_recorded notification.

nodes.label: Connect Athlete Who Already Has an Account
nodes.rationale: The invitation is created for an existing user's phone. Acceptance after OTP finds the user and creates an athlete profile only if missing. If the pair's relationship row exists and is ended, that same row becomes active and a reactivated event is written, subject to capacity. If it is already active, acceptance returns it unchanged. Two coaches inviting the same person create two independent relationships when each has capacity. The existing password is not reset.
nodes.norm_label: connect athlete who already has an account

nodes.label: End the Coaching Relationship
nodes.rationale: The relationship becomes ended, ended_at is filled, and an ended event is inserted. Open invitations and active assignments of that relationship close. Sessions, sets, versions, observations, and messages are not deleted. A new session after this time does not receive this relationship id. The coach may only read messages, progress, and programs of this period. Body photos, including photos from this period, close for the coach and for that coach's AI. Data before started_at and another coach's data stay out of reach. Period capacity frees because only active relationships are counted.

nodes.label: Invite Athlete Without an Account
nodes.rationale: The coach with an active period records phone, name, and national code. The scenario both says that a missing user causes users, athlete profile, and the relationship to be created in that same transaction with capacity locked there, and later says that OTP acceptance creates the user, profile, active relationship, started event, and accepted invitation. An open invite for the same coach and phone returns the same row via the unique invite key. The period row is lockForUpdate before the relationship insert. Two concurrent creates for a new phone: one creates the user and the other must attach that user to the relationship instead of returning an unfamiliar account error.

nodes.label: Log a Session and a Record
nodes.rationale: The athlete creates a session with a civil date and, if a relationship is active, that relationship id. Each real attempt is its own set. On set completion the service reads the previous maximum and writes a record event only if the value is greater, linked to that set. estimated_1rm_g is an extra event beside weight and reps. A free session follows the same rule and receives the active relationship id if sent to the coach. Breaking a record notifies the athlete and that relationship's coach. A later program-version change does not rewrite the logged day or sets.
nodes.norm_label: log a session and a record

nodes.label: Body Photos Are in Scope
nodes.rationale: Body photos are no longer outside the roadmap. They are stored in this version, with coach and AI access only during the active relationship.

nodes.label: D-03 Access After the Relationship Ends
nodes.rationale: Confirmed, and narrower than the previous proposal. Messages, progress, and programs of that period remain for the coach. Photos close after the end. There is no access outside the contract interval.
nodes.norm_label: d-03 access after the relationship ends

nodes.label: Non-Blocking Technical Choices
nodes.rationale: These are not commercial decisions and can be reversed during implementation: Laravel Sanctum for mobile tokens and web cookie sessions, the /api/v1 prefix, nullable columns for conditional unique keys because tests use SQLite, textual coach-knowledge retrieval without a vector database, selling AI as a request count while recording tokens only for cost, civil timezone Asia/Tehran with instants stored in UTC, OTP valid 120 seconds with five attempts and invitations valid 7 days, and versioned formulas bmi_v1 and epley_v1.

nodes.label: Critical Path
nodes.rationale: The critical path is F01, F02, F03, F04, F05, F06, then F07 and F08 in order or after F06, then F09, F10, and F11. F07 may start after F03 in parallel with F04, but unfinished work of the previous stage should not be left open at the same time.

nodes.label: F03 Invitation and Relationship
nodes.rationale: The coach creates a new athlete with phone, name, and national code, or connects an existing athlete, without a duplicate account and without passing capacity. A new athlete receives an SMS. The new account's username is the phone and the initial password is the national code. An existing account's password is not reset. The period row is locked when the relationship is created. A person cannot coach themselves. The last seat under two concurrent creates yields one relationship. Ending the relationship removes photos from the coach while keeping messages, progress, and programs of that period. The initial password is not written to logs.

nodes.label: F05 Workout Program and Assignment
nodes.rationale: The coach builds a versioned program and assigns that version to an active relationship. Requires the workout_programs capability on the active period. Only that relationship's coach writes, and only while the relationship is active. Editing after publish does not change the previous version or the previous assignment. Another coach's exercise cannot be selected.

nodes.label: F06 Workout Session and Records
nodes.rationale: Actual performance is stored separately from the prescription, and a record points at the set that created it. epley_v1 is only an extra event. A weaker record does not create an event. Changing the program does not change old sets. After the relationship ends, writing with that id is forbidden and reading that period's progress is allowed. The record is complete in this stage even without the notification, which F09 attaches.

nodes.label: F08 Body Analysis and Progress
nodes.rationale: Incomplete measurements remain over time, and two dates can be compared without writing zero for a missing value. Coach writes require body_analysis. Contract-period progress stays read-only for that coach after the end. Photos are open to the coach only while the relationship is active, and later to that coach's AI. The platform admin does not read this data. After the relationship ends, the photo API returns 403 for the coach. Body photos are in this stage. Weak-muscle labels are out of scope.

nodes.label: F09 Feedback and Notifications
nodes.rationale: Attributable feedback and internal notes stay separate, and the main events store notifications. If F06 and F08 exist, notifications attach to them. A general relationship notification can be tested with F03 alone. The athlete neither writes nor reads coach_only. A notification is only for the recipient user. The subject must belong to the same relationship. This API has no socket and no free-form chat thread. Operating-system push and a realtime messenger are out of scope.

nodes.label: F11 End-to-End Acceptance
nodes.rationale: The scenario document is exercised on the real API from signup through plan expiry. No new product capability is built. Every scenario includes at least one unauthorized attempt: another coach, another athlete, a user without a period, and a repeated callback. Each of the eleven scenarios has a green feature test. A test that was not run is not reported as passed. Also covers suspending a user in the middle of a relationship.

nodes.label: Scenarios and Data Changes
nodes.rationale: Each scenario states only the data effect of the proposed design. The exact API is built in the matching roadmap stage.

nodes.label: Execution Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Stage ids are fixed. Each stage has a testable result and does not pre-build the next stage's domain. Proposals D-01 through D-08 are the default for their stage unless corrected before it starts. No stage had been started when this document was written.

nodes.label: Coach-Only Notes
nodes.rationale: An internal coach note has visibility coach_only and is not returned by the athlete API. A message both parties can see is shared.

nodes.label: No Self Coaching
nodes.rationale: A person may not have a coaching relationship with themselves.

nodes.label: Personal Record Event
nodes.rationale: A record is traceable to the set that achieved it. The metric comes from the exercise type: max weight, reps, duration, or distance. An event is stored only when that metric is broken. A mutable current-record row is not stored.

nodes.label: Post-Contract Read Access
nodes.rationale: The coach sees only the data of their own contract period. After the relationship ends, messages, progress, and programs that coach gave remain read-only. Body photos close for the coach and for that coach's AI. There is no access before the contract starts. Data is not deleted and stays with the athlete.

nodes.label: Prescription Versus Performance
nodes.rationale: The prescribed program and the performed session are two entities. Three prescribed sets of ten are not stored as the same row as actual sets of 10, 9, and 8.

nodes.label: Tehran Calendar Billing
nodes.rationale: A period is proposed to start at confirmed payment. A one-month end is calculated on the Asia/Tehran calendar and stored in UTC, not by adding 30 days.

nodes.label: Integer Half-Up Arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Nutrition totals, BMI, and Epley use integer half-up so results are reproducible and do not depend on floating point. Epley v1 applies only when weight and reps from 1 to 10 both exist: grams times (1 + reps / 30).

nodes.label: No Routine Product Delete
nodes.rationale: DELETE is not the normal path for product data. Suspension, archive, and status changes replace deletion. Paid orders, published versions, food revisions, relationship events, and record events are kept.

nodes.label: Storage and API Unit Conventions
nodes.rationale: Instant time is UTC datetime. Civil dates use the Asia/Tehran calendar. Money is integer rial. Body weight is stored in grams and API kilograms. Height and girths are stored in millimeters and API centimeters. Conversion happens only at the API edge. Food quantity is grams in both API and item storage because that is what the user enters. Energy is integer kilocalories, macros are integer milligrams, percentages are basis points, and BMI is the value times 100. A missing measurement is the absence of a row. Zero is a real value and does not fill a blank.

nodes.label: Stages Do Not Pre-Build
nodes.rationale: Each stage delivers one testable result and does not implement the next domain early. A new product capability is not built in the final acceptance stage. If a defect can be fixed only by changing the design, that change is written in the document before the code changes.

nodes.label: Stable Stage Identifiers
nodes.rationale: Stage ids stay fixed. A new stage gets a new id and earlier numbers are not renumbered, so work can be ordered without rewriting history.

nodes.label: Athlete
nodes.rationale: The athlete is an athlete_profiles row: a personal panel and the athlete's own data. An athlete may have active relationships with several coaches, with each relationship's data kept separate.

nodes.label: Coach
nodes.rationale: The coach is a coach_profiles row: data scope, plan, athletes, programs, and the assistant.

nodes.label: Fito Coaching SaaS
nodes.rationale: Fito is a coaching SaaS, not a chatbot and not only a program builder. The core value is moving coach and athlete history out of messengers and files so coaching decisions stay tied to real history. AI suggests inside that data boundary; numeric results come from backend data, not from the model guessing.

nodes.label: National Code
nodes.rationale: National code is checked for structure and check digit without an ownership inquiry against the phone. It remains the identity when the password changes. Duplicate national code or phone does not create a second account.

nodes.label: Phone OTP
nodes.rationale: OTP proves phone ownership. A users row is not created until signup completes successfully.

nodes.label: Person
nodes.rationale: The person is the users account: login and ownership of profiles. A product role is not one role column with three fixed values.

nodes.label: otp_challenges
nodes.rationale: A one-time phone challenge for signup, login, or invitation. The code text is not stored, only code_hash. Proposed validity is 120 seconds and at most 5 wrong attempts. Code 12345 is accepted only when APP_ENV=local, and its presence in production is a startup error.

nodes.label: password_reset_tokens
nodes.rationale: Not a product table. Product dependency on it is removed in F01.

nodes.label: personal_access_tokens
nodes.rationale: Created by Sanctum's own migration. Mobile login stores a token here. Web login uses sessions.

nodes.label: sessions
nodes.rationale: Laravel session storage. It is infrastructure, not a product-domain table, and is kept.

nodes.label: signup_drafts
nodes.rationale: An unfinished signup exists before the account. Panel is only coach or athlete. When the draft is consumed, open_phone is set null in the same update so the unique open phone is released.

nodes.label: Coach Signup
nodes.rationale: A normalized phone opens a signup draft and a signup OTP before any user exists. Final signup writes users and only one profile in one transaction, then nulls open_phone. The coach can enter the panel without a paid order. Web login creates a session. Mobile login creates a personal access token. An existing phone or national code fails on the unique constraint so a half-created account does not remain. An athlete panel does not create independent services or a platform payment. A coach's athlete profile is created later, only when they become another coach's athlete.

nodes.label: F01 Corrections to the Skeleton
nodes.rationale: When F01 starts: change users from email and password to phone and national code, remove the product dependency on password_reset_tokens, replace the seeder that creates test@example.com, add API v1, a token guard, and an access policy, and lock production against the fixed OTP.

nodes.label: F01 Identity Profile and Login
nodes.rationale: A person can sign up or log in with OTP, and the account and profile are created together only when signup succeeds. Web uses a session. Mobile uses a token. A suspended user cannot log in. Concurrent duplicate signup creates one user. The fixed OTP makes production refuse to boot. The panel is only coach or athlete. A coach without a plan can still see /me.

nodes.label: Atomic Account and Profile
nodes.rationale: The account and exactly one profile are created in one transaction. Coach self-signup does not require a password. An athlete created by a coach uses the phone as username and the national code as the initial password, both changeable later, with the password stored only as a hash.

nodes.label: Development OTP 12345
nodes.rationale: The fixed code 12345 is accepted only in development. If that fixed code is enabled in production, the service must refuse to boot.

nodes.label: Single Panel at Signup
nodes.rationale: Signup chooses only coach or athlete. There is no both-panel. A coach can later become another coach's athlete, and the athlete profile is created at that moment, not at signup.

nodes.label: AI Assistant
nodes.rationale: The assistant drafts workouts or meals in the coach's method. Output stays a draft until the coach approves it. Tools may read only that coach and that relationship. Athlete access defaults off and depends on the plan. Quota is consumed once if two requests race. The assistant is not a physician.

nodes.label: Body Observation
nodes.rationale: One check-in is one body_observations row at a measurement time. Only metrics that were actually taken get values. Comparison of two dates reads these rows. A private observation is not shown to a coach; a relationship observation is not shown to a different coach.

nodes.label: Body Photo
nodes.rationale: Body photos are in this version. The coach, or the athlete, stores them. The design review's data dictionary limits coach access to an active contract.

nodes.label: Coach-only Note
nodes.rationale: A coach-only note is not the message the athlete sees. The athlete cannot read it. The coach's reply that is shared is separate from this internal note.

nodes.label: Coaching Relationship
nodes.rationale: coaching_relationships is the permission to program and to see data for that collaboration. One row exists per coach-athlete pair. Ending and starting again reuse that same row. After it ends, new writes with that id are closed. Several coaches mean several rows, each with its own coach_profile_id.

nodes.label: F08 Body Analysis
nodes.rationale: Usable result: a partial body analysis, BMI, and a comparison of two dates.

nodes.label: F09 Feedback and Notices
nodes.rationale: Usable result: feedback, coach-only notes, and in-app notices. Not a realtime messenger.

nodes.label: F10 Coach Assistant
nodes.rationale: Usable result: an assistant limited to that coach, with quota and approval before publication.

nodes.label: F11 End-to-end Acceptance
nodes.rationale: Usable result: a test of this whole path with no new capability. No stage had been started when the design review was written.

nodes.label: Relationship Feedback
nodes.rationale: Feedback attaches to a session, a program item, an exercise, or a general subject of that relationship. It is not a realtime chat.

nodes.label: Coaching Relationship Event
nodes.rationale: coaching_relationship_events is append-only. Event types are started, ended, and reactivated.

nodes.label: Coach Approval Before Publish
nodes.rationale: D-06 is a conservative default because the product left AI publication open. Generated programs stay draft until the coach approves. Approval turns the draft into a normal program version; assignment then follows the workout or meal-plan path. Nothing is assigned without that approval. Athlete access to the assistant stays off unless the plan allows it, and that use still spends the coach's quota.

nodes.label: Empty Value Is Not Zero
nodes.rationale: A check-in may be incomplete. Missing metrics do not create a row and are not stored as zero. Zero is a real value. BMI uses bmi_v1 only when height and weight exist, and it is kept beside device data. The product does not label a muscle as weak.

nodes.label: Multi-Coach Data Isolation
nodes.rationale: An athlete may have several coaches at once. Each relationship's data stays separate. Private analysis is not automatically sent to every coach. A coach does not see another coach's athletes, and the athlete does not see the coach's internal notes.

nodes.label: No Self-Coaching
nodes.rationale: A person cannot be their own coach. The database cannot easily express that the two profiles share an owner, so the acceptance transaction rejects it. An experienced coach may still be the athlete of a more experienced coach.

nodes.label: Photo Access During the Active Contract
nodes.rationale: Confirmed D-03, narrower than an earlier proposal: the coach and that coach's assistant see photos only while the relationship is active. After it ends they lose the photos and also cannot see data from before the contract. Chat, progress, and programs from that period stay readable so the coach can review the arc. The athlete keeps their own data. Before the contract starts, the coach has no access.
nodes.norm_label: photo access during the active contract

nodes.label: Reactivate the Same Relationship Row
nodes.rationale: A coach-athlete pair has one relationship row. Ending and starting again updates that row and appends a reactivated event. A second row is not created. Capacity is checked again before reactivation.

nodes.label: Athlete Invitation
nodes.rationale: athlete_invitations is how a coach asks a phone number to join. Statuses are pending, accepted, expired, revoked, and declined. One open invitation per coach and phone. Suggested lifetime is 7 days. Acceptance stores the resulting coaching_relationship_id.

nodes.label: Athlete Profile
nodes.rationale: A user has at most one athlete panel. The athlete sees programs, actual performance, records, allowed body data, and feedback. They do not see the coach's internal notes or how other coaches relate to each other.

nodes.label: F01 Identity and Login
nodes.rationale: Usable result: OTP signup and login, coach or athlete profile, web session, and mobile token. Prerequisite is the current repo. Plan, invitation, and programs are not built in this stage.

nodes.label: National ID
nodes.rationale: National ID is required with the phone number. Only structure and the check digit are validated; ownership of the phone is not queried from a registry.

nodes.label: OTP Challenge
nodes.rationale: Phone login uses a one-time code. The fixed code 12345 is not accepted in production. An expired code or more than five wrong tries is consumed. A suspended user cannot enter. Web receives a session; mobile receives a token.

nodes.label: Laravel Sanctum
nodes.rationale: Sanctum is the proposed, reversible choice for the web cookie session and the mobile token. It is not installed. F01 is expected to create the token table. The API prefix /api/v1 is similarly reversible and not a commercial decision.

nodes.label: Signup Draft
nodes.rationale: signup_drafts and otp_challenges exist before users. No account is created until signup succeeds, so a failed finish leaves no half-built account.

nodes.label: User Account
nodes.rationale: Each person has one account, with phone and national ID. At signup they choose only a coach panel or an athlete panel; there is no combined panel. A coach can later gain an athlete profile when they become a student of another coach. The account and profile are created together only at the successful end of signup. OTP signup does not collect a password. A duplicate phone or national ID must not create a second account.

nodes.label: Acceptance Activates Relationship
nodes.rationale: How an invitation becomes active in UC-03 and UC-04: after OTP, one transaction creates the missing user, athlete profile, and active relationship, writes a started event, and marks the invitation accepted. If capacity is full, the transaction rolls back. If the person already has an account, acceptance only links them. If that pair's relationship had ended, the same row is reactivated instead of inserting a second row. An already active relationship is left unchanged.

nodes.label: Current Laravel Skeleton
nodes.rationale: The review says development has not started and the document is a design proposal, not product code. The repo is Laravel 12 on PHP 8.2 and MySQL, but the framework and Sanctum are not installed, domain tables are not migrated, and the users table still requires a unique email and a password, which conflicts with phone OTP signup. Auth is only the web session guard. One PHPUnit test checks the welcome page. F01 is expected to replace email identity with phone and national ID.

nodes.label: Invitation Without an Account
nodes.rationale: UC-03 and value-flow step 4: the coach invites a phone number while an access period is active. The invitation does not create the user and does not consume capacity yet. A repeat invite from the same coach returns the same open invitation. The phone owner later proves the number with OTP, gives national ID and name, and only then are the account, athlete profile, and relationship created.

nodes.label: Coach-Provisioned Athlete Account
nodes.rationale: The workflow brief, and the design review's confirmed athlete-registration note, say the coach enters phone, name, and national ID. If the person is not in the system, the account is created immediately and an SMS is sent: username is the phone and the initial password is the national ID, changeable after login. The national ID remains the identity. If the account already exists, the person is only linked and the password is not touched. Plan capacity is checked at this step. This conflicts with UC-03, which says the invitation itself creates neither the account nor the capacity use.

nodes.label: Body Measurement
nodes.rationale: body_observation_values are real measurements such as chest girth in millimeters, body-fat percent, and weight. They are a different concept from target muscles and from body-model areas.

nodes.label: Body Model Area
nodes.rationale: body_model_areas is a front-end highlight code. Mapping a muscle to a display area is visual only and is not a body measurement.

nodes.label: Exercise Catalog
nodes.rationale: The platform exercise bank carries instructions, target muscles, and a goal. Adding an exercise to the bank requires admin approval. Program shape is free: a weekday split, full body, or any other grouping.

nodes.label: F06 Session and Records
nodes.rationale: Usable result: actual sessions, free training, and personal records.

nodes.label: Personal Record
nodes.rationale: A record event is stored only when a maximum is broken, and it points at that set. There is no mutable current-record row. Metrics are max weight, duration, distance, reps, and a versioned estimated one-rep max.

nodes.label: Platform Admin
nodes.rationale: Platform admin is a role separate from the coach profile. In version one the admin manages accounts, plans, payments, and suspension, and does not read private training or body content. An admin may also be an ordinary user.

nodes.label: Private Exercise
nodes.rationale: A coach may create a private exercise. Another coach cannot select it. Unowned exercises are the platform catalog. Decision D-07 is confirmed for exercises; private food is the same technical proposal and was not separately rejected.

nodes.label: Workout Session
nodes.rationale: A session is actual performance, not a copy of the prescription. Each performed set is its own row. The session receives the relationship id only when that relationship is active at the start. After the relationship ends, a new session does not take that id. A free session outside the program uses the same record rules.

nodes.label: Record Metric Follows the Exercise
nodes.rationale: Confirmed: a record is not always weight. Depending on the exercise it is weight and reps, reps, duration, or distance. A weaker value is not stored. Estimated one-rep max uses the versioned Epley formula epley_v1 and is extra beside weight and reps. A free workout outside the plan, such as a weekly run, is stored separately and still counts in analysis.

nodes.label: Canonical Storage Units
nodes.rationale: The client enters body weight in kilograms, height and girths in centimeters, and food in grams, and converts before send. Internal body storage is integer grams and millimeters. Food energy is integer kilocalories and macros are milligrams, rounded half-up. Percents use basis points. Instants are stored in UTC; the civil workout date uses Asia/Tehran. Money is an integer rial. Empty input does not insert a row.

nodes.label: F03 Coaching Relationship
nodes.rationale: Usable result: invite an athlete, link an existing athlete, end the relationship, and lock capacity. This is the stage that turns an invitation into an active collaboration.

nodes.label: F04 Exercise Catalog
nodes.rationale: Usable result: exercise catalog, muscles, and body-model areas, including private exercises and an admin-approved request to enter the bank.

nodes.label: F05 Workout Program
nodes.rationale: Usable result: a versioned workout program assigned to an active relationship.

nodes.label: F07 Meal Plan
nodes.rationale: Usable result: foods with nutrient revisions and a meal plan. The food catalog is built here because it is a smaller catalog than exercises.

nodes.label: Food Nutrient Revision
nodes.rationale: Each food edit is a new immutable revision. Changing nutrients does not rewrite a previously published meal plan.

nodes.label: Meal Plan
nodes.rationale: The coach writes food in grams. Published meal items point at a nutrient revision. Energy and macros are computed on read. Actual food intake has no table in this version.

nodes.label: Published Program Version
nodes.rationale: Publishing locks the version. Assignment connects the athlete to that version, not to a future latest edit. A later edit is a new version.

nodes.label: Workout Assignment
nodes.rationale: Assignment binds one published version to one active coaching relationship. Older assignments keep pointing at their own version.

nodes.label: Immutable Published History
nodes.rationale: The program on paper is not the same object as what was performed. Editing a workout creates a new version; earlier sessions stay on the old version. The same pattern applies to food: a later nutrient change does not rewrite a previously published plan. Payments, published versions, relationship events, and record events are not deleted or rewritten.

nodes.label: Access Period
nodes.rationale: The access period is created only after the gateway confirms the order amount. A coach has one active period at a time. When it ends, new invites and new writes lock; history is not deleted.

nodes.label: Athlete Capacity
nodes.rationale: Capacity is the plan's athlete seat count, enforced on the access period with a row lock. Two simultaneous accepts for the last seat create only one relationship.

nodes.label: F02 Plan and Payment
nodes.rationale: Usable result: admin-defined plans, an order, a non-repeatable payment, and an access period. Until payment, the panel stays in tour mode.

nodes.label: Payment
nodes.rationale: Each payment attempt is its own row. Only a confirmed amount equal to the order creates one payment and one access period. A repeated callback does not create a second subscription. An amount mismatch grants no access. A coach has only one open order at a time.

nodes.label: Subscription Plan
nodes.rationale: Price, duration, athlete capacity, features, and AI quota are not hardcoded. The admin defines them. A later price change does not alter an earlier purchase.

nodes.label: Expiry Does Not Auto-Drop Athletes
nodes.rationale: D-04 is still a proposal. When the period expires, new writes close. Lowering capacity does not automatically end active relationships; further invites and reactivations are rejected until the count fits. Reason: dropping an athlete automatically is a heavy commercial decision and is not in the product definition. No paused status, no bank auto-renewal, and no installment of a price difference in this version.

nodes.label: Pay Later Tour Lock
nodes.rationale: The coach may choose pay later at signup. The panel opens immediately, without a required password, so they can look around. Creating athletes, programs, nutrition, analysis, and AI stays locked until a purchase is confirmed.

nodes.label: Platform Fee Not Athlete Tuition
nodes.rationale: The coach pays the platform for software service. The financial contract between coach and athlete stays outside Fito. Athlete payment to the platform is a future feature. Stored money is an integer rial amount so the gateway is not given a decimal or an ambiguous toman figure. If the sales UI shows toman, conversion by ten happens only at that edge. A later plan price does not change a completed purchase.

nodes.label: Pay Later Tour
nodes.rationale: A new coach may choose pay later, see the panel as a tour, and keep plan features locked until a plan is purchased.

nodes.label: Plans Orders and Access
nodes.rationale: Plan definition, order, payment attempt, confirmed payment, access period, and quota consumption are separate. One order has many payment attempts. A repeated callback does not create a second access period. Price and features must stay traceable after a later plan change.

nodes.label: access_periods
nodes.rationale: The access window, athlete capacity, and AI quota. A coach has at most one active period, enforced by unique active_coach_id. Capacity and quota are decided with lockForUpdate on this row.

nodes.label: order_features
nodes.rationale: The feature snapshot of that order, so a later plan edit does not rewrite what was bought.

nodes.label: orders
nodes.rationale: The order and the frozen picture of purchase terms. A coach has at most one pending order, enforced by a unique open_checkout_coach_id. After paid, snapshot columns do not change.

nodes.label: payment_attempts
nodes.rationale: Each gateway attempt. Amount must equal the order. gateway manual is only an admin-recorded payment and follows the same activation path. gateway_payload is raw and is not the commercial source of truth.

nodes.label: payments
nodes.rationale: Confirmed money. Each order has at most one confirmed payment. A repeated callback hits this unique constraint and does not create a second period.

nodes.label: plan_features
nodes.rationale: Current features of a plan definition. Known feature keys are a closed set in code so a typo cannot create a new capability.

nodes.label: plans
nodes.rationale: The editable plan definition for future sales. Editing this table changes only later sales. A sold plan is not deleted; selling stops with is_sellable. A paid order keeps its own snapshot.

nodes.label: Plan Expiry or Plan Change
nodes.rationale: A job moves an active period whose ends_at has passed to expired and nulls active_coach_id. A due scheduled period becomes active in the same process if the active key stays unique. After expiry with no replacement, invitations, new assignments, AI generation, and coaching writes are rejected. History remains readable as in the end-relationship scenario. A new plan purchase creates a new order and snapshot. If the proposed policy starts it after the current period, a scheduled period is created. If the new capacity is below the active relationship count, no relationship is automatically ended. A failed payment only marks the attempt failed. The order can accept a new attempt until it expires. A repeated failed callback does not create a payment or a period.

nodes.label: Plan Purchase and Access Activation
nodes.rationale: An existing pending order is returned; otherwise the order and feature snapshot are copied from the current plan. Each payment start is a new attempt with a unique idempotency key. The callback locks the attempt. If a payment already exists, nothing new is inserted. The confirmed amount must equal the order price or the attempt fails and no period is created. Success writes one payment, marks the order paid, clears the open-checkout key, and creates one access period. If no other period is active, the new period is active; otherwise it is scheduled to start when the active period ends. Later plan edits do not change snapshotted order rows.

nodes.label: D-02 Rial or Toman
nodes.rationale: Proposal: store money and charge the gateway in integer rial. If the sales UI shows toman, convert only at that edge with a factor of 10. Amounts must not be decimal or ambiguous, and Iranian gateways usually take rial. Five million toman and five million rial differ by ten times. Columns are named *_irr. If rejected, money column names and units change before F02. Order logic does not fundamentally change.

nodes.label: D-04 Expiry and Excess Capacity
nodes.rationale: Proposal: expiry closes new writes. Lower capacity does not automatically end active relationships; invitations and reactivation are rejected until the count fits. No proration and no automatic bank renewal. Automatic cutoff is a heavy commercial decision and is not in the product definition. A new paused status is not added to the relationship. If rejected, the status and the order of choosing excess athletes must be specified before F03.

nodes.label: D-05 Analysis Visibility Across Coaches
nodes.rationale: Proposal: an observation is either private to the athlete or attached to one relationship. A second coach does not see it automatically. The product asked to separate personal data from relationship data and allows several coaches. The effect is a visibility column on body_observations. If rejected, the observation rule must be simplified before F08, and the visibility column might be removed.

nodes.label: D-08 Real Gateway
nodes.rationale: The payment model should not depend on a gateway name. Until a gateway and merchant are chosen, F02 builds the domain path, idempotent callback, and a test gateway. The real connection is not that stage. Missing a gateway name does not stop the table design.

nodes.label: F02 Plans Orders Payments and Periods
nodes.rationale: An admin creates plans and a coach with a successful payment receives exactly one access period. Until then the panel is a tour and plan features stay locked. The real commercial gateway is out of scope. A test gateway and an audited manual admin payment are in scope. Two concurrent callbacks create one payment and one period. A monthly period uses the Tehran calendar.
nodes.norm_label: f02 plans orders payments and periods

nodes.label: Open Decision Label
nodes.rationale: An open decision can still change behavior or tables before its stage.

nodes.label: Proposal Label
nodes.rationale: A proposal is the default design for implementation and is not a final commercial decision.

nodes.label: Capacity Lock at Acceptance
nodes.rationale: Athlete capacity is locked at acceptance and reactivation, not when the invitation is created. Two concurrent acceptances for the last seat: one succeeds and the other is rejected. When a period ends, new coaching writes and new invitations close, but relationships and history are not deleted. Dropping capacity does not automatically end athletes; while active relationships exceed capacity, new invitations and reactivations are rejected.

nodes.label: Immutable Financial and Version History
nodes.rationale: Duplicate accounts are closed by a unique constraint and a transaction. Financial history, program versions, and food revisions are not deleted or rewritten. Concurrent capacity and payment decisions are made inside a transaction.

nodes.label: Rial Integer Money
nodes.rationale: Proposed currency is integer rial because common Iranian gateways charge in rial. Five million toman, if the price is in toman, equals 50,000,000 rial. That conversion is still an open commercial decision and must not stay ambiguous in the UI.

nodes.label: JSON Only for Non-Truth Payloads
nodes.rationale: JSON is used only for ai_generations.proposal, because the draft is variable and is not the source of truth before it becomes program rows, and for payment_attempts.gateway_payload, because the raw gateway body has no product structure. Sets, meals, prices, plan features, and access are not JSON.

nodes.label: Row Lock for Capacity and Quota
nodes.rationale: Capacity and quota are decided by lockForUpdate on the access period. The usage counter and the usage ledger commit together, or not at all.
nodes.norm_label: row lock for capacity and quota

nodes.label: Coach Profile
nodes.rationale: The coach profile is the ownership boundary for athletes, programs, plans, payments, and the assistant. A user has at most one coach profile.

nodes.label: Coach AI Workspace
nodes.rationale: coach_ai_workspaces is per coach and holds method, preferences, knowledge, and conversations. It is not the product data boundary. Knowledge chunks repeat coach_profile_id so retrieval must filter on it.

nodes.label: Coach Profile Data Boundary
nodes.rationale: Confirmed D-01: there is no gym and no branch. The working scope is the coach profile. Plans, payments, athletes, programs, and the assistant attach to that profile. The AI workspace only names that coach's memory; it is not an organization and not a second ownership boundary. Every coach-domain query stays inside coach_profile_id.

nodes.label: Shared Model, Private Memory
nodes.rationale: The assistant is not a separately trained model per coach. The model is shared, but memory, preferences, method, and workspace stay with that coach, and programs are built in that method. Numbers are computed from real data. The assistant does not guess and does not show one coach's or athlete's information to another coach.

nodes.label: Fito
nodes.rationale: Fito is a coaching SaaS, not a chatbot and not only a workout builder. A coach buys a platform subscription, brings their own athletes, and for those relationships provides workout plans, meal plans, actual-performance tracking, body analysis, and an AI assistant. The athlete has a personal panel. The platform admin runs accounts, plans, and payments. The product problem is scattered history across messengers, program files, and notes.

nodes.label: Design Status Labels
nodes.rationale: Four labels stay fixed: product need, proposal, open decision, and not in code, plus future. A proposal is only a default so version one can be built; if it is corrected before the related stage, that stage changes. An open decision is not the user's choice yet and affects money, data privacy, or AI publication. Future items are outside this version and have no stage id. No commercial proposal is written down as a final decision. Where the opening summary conflicts with the data dictionary or the execution map, those appendices govern tables and stages. The confirmed-corrections section overrides older sentences in the same file.

nodes.label: Version-One Exclusions
nodes.rationale: No stage id is assigned to actual food intake, independent athlete services without a coach, athlete tuition and settlement, realtime chat, a coach marketplace, or gym management. The workflow brief also excludes athlete payment to the platform and an AI program without a coach. The design review later says body photos are no longer outside the roadmap; access still follows the active contract.

nodes.label: Public Crawler Policy
nodes.rationale: robots.txt addresses every user agent and sets Disallow to an empty value, which is the conventional allow-all crawler policy.

nodes.label: Flutter Mobile Clients
nodes.rationale: The product is consumed on the web and later on Android and iOS. Both clients use the same API. The mobile version is built with Flutter.

nodes.label: cache
nodes.rationale: Laravel cache and cache_locks. They are infrastructure, not product-domain tables, and are kept.

nodes.label: jobs
nodes.rationale: Laravel jobs, job_batches, and failed_jobs. They are infrastructure, not product-domain tables, and are kept.

nodes.label: MySQL Target Engine
nodes.rationale: The target engine is MySQL. The project's default tests use in-memory SQLite.

nodes.label: Laravel 12 Skeleton
nodes.rationale: This backend is a Laravel 12 skeleton. composer.json has only laravel/framework and laravel/tinker. Migrations are the default users, cache, and jobs set. Routes are web.php and console.php and return the Laravel welcome page. The only feature test is HTTP 200 on the home page. .env.example has no product settings beyond Laravel defaults. The local .env names a MySQL connection to a database called Fito. No old product document was found in the repo, and no old ban on designing the whole product was found, which is why this design is not limited to OTP.

nodes.label: Preserved Stack
nodes.rationale: Keep Laravel 12, PHP 8.2, MySQL as the target engine, PHPUnit, and in-memory SQLite for tests. Keep sessions, cache, cache_locks, jobs, job_batches, and failed_jobs. Keep the migration and Eloquent pattern. If the initial users migration has already run, F01 does not rewrite history; the change is a new migration.

nodes.label: App Models User
nodes.rationale: The only product model is App\Models\User with name, email, and password. Reported minimal signup does not match the repository: users.password is required, uniqueness is on email, only the web session guard exists, and Sanctum and routes/api.php are absent.

nodes.label: Implemented Label
nodes.rationale: Implemented means the behavior already exists in this backend repository.

nodes.label: Product Need Label
nodes.rationale: A product need is explicit in the current product definition.

nodes.label: Shared Web and Mobile API
nodes.rationale: The Laravel backend is the shared API for web, Android, and iOS.

nodes.label: Entity Relationship Diagrams
nodes.rationale: The diagrams are the same model as the database design, split by domain for readability. users is repeated so each domain boundary stays visible. Line labels are English relationship names so right-to-left print does not scramble them.

nodes.label: Repository Status and Open Decisions
nodes.rationale: Reviewed on 9 October 2026 from files in this backend repository. The mysql command was not on PATH and vendor was not installed, so the live Fito database was not inspected. The result is file status only.

nodes.label: Fito Backend Product Design
nodes.rationale: Stage-one design with decisions confirmed on 10 October 2026. Implementation has not started. Approved decisions in the status document override earlier proposals.

nodes.label: Laravel Framework README
nodes.rationale: The stock Laravel README introduces the framework. The product status doc says it is not a Fito domain decision and has not been rewritten.

nodes.label: Nullable Conditional Unique Key
nodes.rationale: A conditional unique key is a nullable column maintained by the domain service, not a MySQL-only generated column, so the same schema can be tested on SQLite. Multiple NULLs are allowed in a unique index.

nodes.label: Signup Report Conflict
nodes.rationale: An important conflict: a report that minimal signup was implemented does not match the repository. The file status, not that report, is the basis for what must be built.

nodes.label: ai_conversations
nodes.rationale: A conversation scoped to a coach, optionally a relationship and athlete, pinned to a setting version. Audience is coach or athlete. An athlete conversation is created only when ai_athlete_access is on the active period of that relationship's coach.

nodes.label: ai_generations
nodes.rationale: A structured proposal before publication. Kind is workout program, meal plan, or progress review. Status is draft, approved, rejected, or materialized. proposal JSON is not the source of truth after materialize. Coach approval creates ordinary program-version rows and records their ids here. Assignment uses the normal training-domain rules after the version exists.

nodes.label: ai_messages
nodes.rationale: A conversation turn or tool result. Role is user, assistant, or tool. Initial tools are relationship_summary, workout_history, personal_records, body_series, shared_feedback, coach_method, and knowledge_search. Each tool takes the coach id and, when present, the relationship id from the server context, not from user text.

nodes.label: Allowed AI Tools
nodes.rationale: Closed initial tool set: relationship_summary, workout_history, personal_records, body_series, shared_feedback, coach_method, knowledge_search. Identifiers come from server context. User text cannot select another coach or a new tool.

nodes.label: ai_usage_entries
nodes.rationale: The ledger of AI quota use. Incrementing ai_requests_used and inserting a usage entry are one transaction. If quota is insufficient, neither is written. Provider tokens are stored only to observe cost. The sales unit is the request.

nodes.label: athlete_profiles
nodes.rationale: The athlete panel. One athlete profile per user. Gender and birth date were not requested and have no columns.

nodes.label: coach_ai_setting_versions
nodes.rationale: Versioned methodology, preferences, and constraints. A published row does not change. A conversation points at the version of that time. Completing the first version fills the coach's ai_onboarding_completed_at.

nodes.label: coach_ai_workspaces
nodes.rationale: Per-coach memory on the shared model: method, interests, knowledge, and conversations. This workspace is not the data boundary of the whole product. The data boundary remains coach_profiles. One workspace per coach.

nodes.label: coach_knowledge_chunks
nodes.rationale: A retrievable text chunk. coach_profile_id is repeated on purpose so the filter is mandatory. Retrieval with no coach_profile_id returns empty. MySQL FULLTEXT is not tested on SQLite. Document text is data and does not grant tool permission or change the coach.

nodes.label: coach_knowledge_documents
nodes.rationale: A coach knowledge document, unique per coach and sha256. The coach may remove their own document from retrieval. Earlier messages keep their own text.

nodes.label: coach_profiles
nodes.rationale: The coach data-ownership boundary. Also holds current_ai_setting_version_id and ai_onboarding_completed_at so a separate one-to-one table is not created. One coach profile per user.

nodes.label: Feature ai_athlete_access
nodes.rationale: Athlete access to the assistant. It is a plan capability. When enabled, the athlete conversation still spends the coach's period quota.

nodes.label: users
nodes.rationale: The person account. Email is not a product field. Self-signup with OTP does not require a password. If a coach creates an athlete, password is the hash of the national code and password_is_initial is true. Changing the password does not change national_code. Physical deletion is not in the first version; suspension only changes status.

nodes.label: AI Proposal and Publication
nodes.rationale: Generative requests are rejected while ai_onboarding_completed_at is empty. Creating a turn locks the active period, increments quota by one, and writes a usage entry. Tools read only that coach_profile_id and the context relationship. Model text is stored on messages. A program output is a draft generation with a proposal and is not assigned. Coach approval builds an ordinary workout or meal version, marks the generation materialized, and stores the version id. Assignment then follows the workout or meal scenario. Rejection marks the generation rejected and builds no version. An athlete can open a conversation only if ai_athlete_access is on the period snapshot, and it spends that coach's quota.

nodes.label: D-01 Coach Profile Scope
nodes.rationale: Confirmed. coach_profiles is the ownership boundary. Workspace is only the name of that coach's AI memory, not a gym entity. There is no gym.

nodes.label: D-06 Coach Approves AI Output
nodes.rationale: Proposal: AI output is not assigned until the coach approves it. Athlete access to the assistant defaults off and depends on a plan capability. That quota is also taken from the coach's period. The product left these open, and the first version should be conservative and implementable. The effect is ai_generations statuses and the ai_athlete_access key. If rejected, F10 changes the publish path or the conversation audience, and that should be said before that stage.

nodes.label: F10 Coach Assistant
nodes.rationale: The model stays shared, each coach has a memory workspace, and workout and nutrition proposals are built in that coach's method. The photo tool works only for an active relationship. The model gateway sits behind an interface that tests can replace. Every tool is filtered by the server's coach id. User text does not choose a new tool or another coach. Generation is closed without onboarding. Exhausted quota rolls the transaction back. Two requests for the last quota unit consume only one. An unapproved proposal creates no assignment. Another coach's knowledge chunk is not in the tool result. Record and BMI numbers come from database tools. A dedicated model, web search, a vector database, and medical prescription are out of scope.

nodes.label: Coach Approves AI Programs
nodes.rationale: Proposed initial policy, not yet a final decision: an AI program is not assigned to the athlete without coach approval. Direct athlete access to the assistant is a plan capability and defaults off. If it is on, quota comes from that coach's period and the conversation is limited to that coach's relationships. Until the coach records a working method, generative tools stay closed. A successful assistant turn consumes one request from the period quota. Provider tokens are recorded for cost, but the sales unit is the request, not the token.

nodes.label: AI Tool and Data Limits
nodes.rationale: The assistant does not go to unrelated topics or uncontrolled sources. The limit is in tools and data, not only in prompt text. User content does not change access rules. The system is not a substitute for a physician. Athlete photos and data reach a tool only inside the active relationship of that coach. Numbers and comparisons inside tools come from SQL and application logic. Free web search, a vector database, and a dedicated model are not in this version. Retrieval is textual and limited to the coach.

nodes.label: AI Workspace Is Memory Only
nodes.rationale: The word workspace is only the per-coach AI memory. It is not the ownership boundary of product data.

nodes.label: Coach Profile Data Boundary
nodes.rationale: Confirmed: the working data scope is coach_profiles. There is no gym, branch, or organizational workspace. One coach's data and settings are separated from another's by coach_profile_id. Plans and payments attach to the coach profile, not to the person alone and not to the athlete. The athlete keeps an independent identity and connects to coaches through relationships. Personal athlete data is not mixed with data created inside a relationship.

nodes.label: Shared Model Per-Coach Memory
nodes.rationale: All coaches share one model. A separate model is not trained per coach. Each coach has a memory workspace for interests, method, and working knowledge, and programs must be built in that method.

nodes.label: Rules Enforced in the Transaction
nodes.rationale: The database holds keys, uniqueness, and not-null. The application transaction checks the national-code digit, phone normalization, atomic user and profile creation, payment amount equality, one-time period activation, the period lock, the ban on self-coaching, assignment matching the relationship, published-version and revision locks, tracking-type columns, half-up math, not writing zero for null, coach_only and coach_profile_id filters, and turning an AI proposal into relationship rows only after coach approval.

nodes.label: One Relationship Row Per Pair
nodes.rationale: One coach and athlete pair has only one relationship row. Several coaches for one athlete are several rows with different coach_profile_id values.

nodes.label: BMI v1
nodes.rationale: Calculated BMI is written only when the observation's weight and a valid height at that time or earlier exist. bmi_v1 is kilograms divided by height in meters squared, stored as BMI times 100. A device BMI is stored separately with origin measured.

nodes.label: Body and Progress
nodes.rationale: Measurements may be incomplete. Zero is not a stand-in for a missing value. API body weight is kilograms and heights and girths are centimeters. Food is entered in grams. If internal storage uses grams and millimeters, conversion happens only at the API edge.

nodes.label: Exercise Catalog and Prescribed Program
nodes.rationale: Programs link to the platform exercise bank or to the coach's private exercises. The coach chooses the program shape, including weekday or full-body sections. Several programs may be active for one athlete. Editing creates a new version and does not rewrite execution history.

nodes.label: Exercise Bank Request
nodes.rationale: A coach may request that an exercise be added to the platform bank. It is inserted only after a platform admin reviews it.

nodes.label: Platform Admin
nodes.rationale: The platform admin, via platform_roles, manages users, plans, payments, and service status. In the first version the admin has no operational access to private training, body data, or coach notes.

nodes.label: Private Coach Exercise
nodes.rationale: A coach may create a private exercise that is not in the platform bank and is usable only by that coach.

nodes.label: Closed Tracking Types
nodes.rationale: Execution type is a closed set: weight_reps, reps, duration, distance. Irrelevant metric columns stay null. Not every exercise is a weighted lift.

nodes.label: body_model_areas
nodes.rationale: Display region of the body model. The code is a frontend contract and is correctable seed data until the frontend repository is available.

nodes.label: exercise_muscles
nodes.rationale: Muscles involved in an exercise, primary or secondary. Unique per exercise and muscle.

nodes.label: exercise_requests
nodes.rationale: A coach request, suggestion, or note for the platform bank. The bank exercise is not created until an admin approves it.

nodes.label: exercises
nodes.rationale: A platform or private exercise. Null coach_profile_id means the platform catalog. An exercise used in a published version is not deleted. Tracking type is weight_reps, reps, duration, or distance.

nodes.label: muscle_body_area
nodes.rationale: Maps a muscle to a display area. The mapping is display only and is not a body measurement.

nodes.label: muscles
nodes.rationale: Target muscle of an exercise, with an optional parent muscle.

nodes.label: platform_roles
nodes.rationale: The initial role value is platform_admin. Unique on user and role.

nodes.label: D-07 Exercise and Food Catalogs
nodes.rationale: Confirmed for exercises: a platform bank plus private exercises, and an admin-approved request to enter the bank. Private food is still a technical proposal of the same pattern and has not been separately rejected.

nodes.label: F04 Exercise Catalog
nodes.rationale: Platform exercises and a coach's private exercises, with muscles and media, are ready for later use. A period and a relationship are not required. Writing the platform catalog is admin-only in this stage. A private exercise is absent from another coach's list. Target muscle is independent of the body-model area and of measurement metrics.

nodes.label: Muscle Area and Metric Split
nodes.rationale: Three concepts stay separate: target muscles for exercise planning, body-model display areas as a frontend contract, and measurements for charts and reports. Labels such as weak muscle are not product facts and have no rule table. Body-model area codes must match the frontend; until that repo is available to this backend, the code list is correctable seed data, not a final contract.

nodes.label: Derived Dashboard
nodes.rationale: The dashboard report has no table of its own. Reports are read from domain entities. Session, set, analysis, and message growth is controlled by time indexes and pagination. Service splits and partitioning are not in the first version.

nodes.label: Actual Food Intake
nodes.rationale: Logging food the athlete actually ate is a future proposal and has no table. A prescribed meal plan is not assumed to be actual intake.

nodes.label: Nutrition Programs
nodes.rationale: A meal plan needs food, quantity and unit, optional day, meal, items, energy, and macros, assigned to an athlete. The basis must be explicit: per 100 grams or per unit. Changing a food must not change the report of a previous plan.

nodes.label: food_nutrient_revisions
nodes.rationale: Immutable nutrient basis. Editing a food inserts a new row and advances current_revision_id. Basis is per_100g or per_unit. Item math uses integer half-up so a later food edit cannot change an old plan.

nodes.label: foods
nodes.rationale: Food identity. Null coach_profile_id means the platform catalog, the same ownership shape as exercises.

nodes.label: meal_assignments
nodes.rationale: Assigns a published meal-plan version to a relationship, with the same shape as workout assignments.

nodes.label: meal_items
nodes.rationale: A meal item pinned to a nutrient revision. Exactly one of quantity_g or quantity_unit_milli is filled, matching the revision basis. No stored total, so the sum cannot drift from the revision.

nodes.label: meal_plan_versions
nodes.rationale: Immutable published meal-plan version. Unique version number per plan. Structure and publish lock match workout program versions.

nodes.label: meal_plans
nodes.rationale: Stable identity of a meal plan. Publish lock matches the training-program structure.

nodes.label: meals
nodes.rationale: A meal on a day. Meal type is breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack, or other.

nodes.label: Create and Assign a Meal Plan
nodes.rationale: A food change gets a new nutrient revision. The previous revision is not updated. Draft items point at the revision current when the item was added. Publishing locks the version. Later food changes attach only future versions to the new revision. Meal assignment points at the relationship and the published version, like workout assignment. Meal calorie totals are not a stored column and are computed on read.
nodes.norm_label: create and assign a meal plan

nodes.label: Outside the Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Actual food intake, athlete payment to the platform, independent athlete service entry, choosing a coach from a public list, an AI program without a coach, settlement, a marketplace, realtime chat, and gym management have no stage id. Body photos are no longer outside the map.

nodes.label: F07 Nutrition
nodes.rationale: A meal plan with an explicit basis and a stable nutrition history is assigned to the athlete. Requires nutrition_programs. The food catalog's ownership matches F04 and is built in this stage because it is a smaller domain than exercises. A food change after publish does not change the previous plan's totals. Exactly one of gram quantity or unit quantity is filled. Half-up rounding is reproducible. Actual intake is out of scope.

nodes.label: Future Label
nodes.rationale: Future means explicitly outside the current version and has no stage id.

nodes.label: Immutable Food Revision
nodes.rationale: Each food edit creates a new immutable revision. A meal item points at that revision. Meal totals are computed on read, with integer half-up rounding, from quantity times the revision.

nodes.label: Platform Fee Only
nodes.rationale: Payment in this version is only the coach's fee for using the platform. The financial contract between coach and athlete stays outside Fito. Athlete payment to the platform is a future feature.

nodes.label: Intentionally Unbuilt Tables
nodes.rationale: Actual food intake, athlete payment to the platform, tuition and the private coach-athlete contract, settlement, gym and branch, realtime chat, a separate AI model per coach, and a table per dashboard chart are deliberately not created. Body photos and per-coach AI memory are in scope. An organizational workspace is not created.

nodes.label: Design Boundary
nodes.rationale: Gym branches, attendance, equipment, realtime chat, a coach marketplace, athlete tuition settlement, and independent athlete services without a coach have no table and no stage in this design.
